description: Front (a): the figure-eight cyclotomic term T_n(q) = prod (1-q^j)(1-q^-j) is EXACTLY bar-invariant (T_n(1/q) = T_n(q)), because the involution merely swaps the two brackets of each factor. Measured at the substrate pair: max relative |T_n(q0)/T_n(1/q0) - 1| = 5.9e-49 over n=1..40, and the closed form -(q^j-1)^2/q^j matches to 1.6e-50. So J(4_1)'s series diverges at q0 and 1/q0 at the SAME rate, and 1/q0 is NOT a better evaluation point — correcting the PR #5084 framing, which was right for a generic q-series but wrong for this invariant: the building block (q;q)_n is asymmetric, but J(4_1) multiplies the two branches and the asymmetry cancels. A state integral (convergent on C\R, not a series in q) is therefore the ONLY route for front (a), not one among several. Scope-(b) for the series route; says nothing about (H1).

assertions.name: inv_q0_is_not_a_better_evaluation_point
assertions.detail: corrects the PR #5084 framing; state integral is the only route

context.corrects: PR #5084 / QOU.QBeta.HabiroEvaluationTrichotomy's closing framing that 1/q0 is the convergent member of the bar-pair. True of the building block, false of J(4_1).
context.scope: Scope-(b) for the SERIES route, invariant named: the bar involution fixes each cyclotomic factor, hence each term. It does not touch (H1) and does not argue against the state-integral route — it narrows front (a) to that route.
